title: Equality of two stripping procedures
statement: The partial function that returns the prefix before the last $1$ in a binary string, and is undefined when there is no $1$, equals the partial function that recursively strips a marked certificate by the same rule.
replaced:
Let $\mathrm{strip}$ be the partial map on binary strings defined by:
$\mathrm{strip}(\varepsilon)$ is undefined, and for a bit $b$ and a string $v$,
$\mathrm{strip}(bv) = b\,\mathrm{strip}(v)$ when $\mathrm{strip}(v)$ is defined,
while otherwise $\mathrm{strip}(1v) = \varepsilon$ and $\mathrm{strip}(0v)$ is
undefined. Let $\mathrm{last}(v)$ be computed by reversing $v$, discarding the
leading $0$s of the reversal, and, if a $1$ remains, deleting it and returning the
reversal of what follows it, while $\mathrm{last}(v)$ is undefined if no $1$
remains. Then $\mathrm{last}$ and $\mathrm{strip}$ are equal as partial maps on
$\{0,1\}^{*}$.
